newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares sharply lower in early bourse trade.
newsitem.headline: German shares sharply lower in early bourse trade.

text.p: Germany's 30-share blue-chip DAX index kicked off bourse trade on Friday sharply lower with traders in Frankfurt seeking inspiration to give direction and cure the hangover from the record run of recent days.

The DAX index fell below the 3,400-point level early on to 3,380.10 points, down 37.50 points, around the level of its electronic IBIS DAX colleague, with little in the way of data to allow the market forge any significant new gains.
"There isn't very much going on this morning and we don't expect to go back over 3,400 points while we are waiting for U.S. data this afternoon," said a Frankfurt trader.
The main focus of attention was on the U.S. February payrolls report due at 1330 GMT.
Shares in engineering group Deutz AG jumped almost 33 percent in bourse trade after a newsletter reported that the company would return to profit in 1997.
The shares were quoted up 2.74 marks at 11.20 marks at 1013 GMT.

The Platow Brief newsletter reported that Deutz, formerly called Kloeckner-Humboldt-Deutz AG and rescued in a one billion-mark bail-out last year, would forecast a profit at its annual results conference on May 15.

Meanwhile shares in medical group Fresenius AG were lower after it denied media reports that it plans to issue bonus shares. Preference shares in Fresenius were down 12 marks at 378 marks in early trade.
